name: McCauley 1A170E/JHA7660, 2-blade fixed pitch, 76 in, 60 in pitch (Cessna 172S, Lycoming IO-360-L2A)

sourced.blades_diameter_pitch: 2 blades, 76 in, 60 in pitch, elliptical tip: Textron Aviation parts page 1A170E-JHA7660
sourced.blade_angle_from_pitch: 60 in at 0.75R is 18.5 deg: atan(60 / (0.75 pi 76)); used as the face angle of the measured maps, and with the 0.75 deg face offset as the blade-element blade's angle
sourced.measured: NACA TR 640 (Hartman & Biermann 1938), 2-blade Clark-Y propeller 5868-9, 10 ft, in front of a liquid-cooled engine nacelle; C_T is effective thrust (shaft tension less the body's slipstream drag increment). Columns as digitised by the c172p-team (FlightGear) in Engines/prop_76in2f_NACA_15-25deg.xml; the static column checks against TR 640 Fig. 43 (Te D / Q = 10.0 at 20 deg, Ct/Cp 1.59).

provenance.stand_in: The McCauley blade's section and planform are not published. Below J 0.3 the TR 640 5868-9 Clark-Y blade's measured maps stand in for it. From J 0.4 up the maps are propeller_bem.py's of a 60 in constant-pitch helix with the 5868-9 planform (TR 640 Fig. 2) scaled in chord, where TR 640 validates the blade-element model (propeller_check.py).
provenance.not_met: The McCauley's Cp(J) is flatter than any 5868-9 blade angle gives: the blade-element blade needs about 27 % more Ct and Cp than the measured 5868-9 at cruise J while the TCDS static band holds its static Cp near the 5868-9's, so the stitched maps step up 10-13 % between J 0.3 and 0.4; recorded in performance/validation.json until McCauley data replaces the stand-in.

fitted.chord_scale: 1.27 (peak chord/diameter 0.096 against the 5868-9's 0.076): fitted with the airframe's CD0 and induced-drag factor to the POH climbs, cruise speeds and fuel flows and the TCDS static run-up; no McCauley chord or activity factor is available
fitted.blade_angle_deg: searched within 18.5-19.5 deg (the sourced 18.5 plus the flat-face convention), landing on the sourced 18.5

assumed.face_offset_deg: 0.75 deg between TR 640's flat-face blade angle and the blade-element tool's reference, the offset that reproduces 5868-9 at 15, 20 and 25 deg
assumed.mach_fade: the tip-Mach power loss fades linearly to nothing at J 0.6; TR 639 confines the loss to take-off and climb but gives no fade law in this form

tip_mach_correction.source: NACA TR 684 (Hartman & Biermann 1940) Fig. 18, 2-blade 5868-9 at V/nD = 0: (Ct/Cp)/(Ct/Cp at M 0.5) about 0.92 at 17.5 deg and 0.96 at 20 deg for tip Mach 0.7, as read by the research-takeoff review; TR 640's tables were measured at tip Mach 0.47-0.56. The JHA7660 turns 2,300-2,400 rpm static, tip Mach 0.69-0.71 at sea level.
